macro: Risk-off tone dominates as Middle East tensions escalate: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz remains shut until the U.S. meets interim-deal conditions, the UAE reported two missiles launched from Iran, and a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait, keeping oil bid. U.S. bond yields are surging — the 30-year hit its highest level since 2007 — pressuring equities, with a tech selloff pulling Wall Street to two-week lows. Trump said no talks with Iran are planned or scheduled, while the dollar stayed range-bound as markets price a dovish Fed response. July data showed the housing market still under pressure even as factory output rose.
internals_narrative: Energy led sectors (+1.0%) with oil-levered names like DVN (+3.8%), PSX (+3.0%) and EOG (+2.5%) among top gainers, while Communication Services (-2.2%), Consumer Staples (-2.1%) and Technology (-1.7%) lagged; CHTR (-6.6%), STZ (-6.2%) and NOW (-5.1%) were the biggest decliners as rising yields hit rate-sensitive and growth names.

ticker_notes.DVN: Devon, Diamondback, Western Midstream and WhiteWater took a positive final investment decision on their Solitude Pipeline System JV to build two 48-inch natural gas pipelines.
ticker_notes.EOG: Barclays maintained Equal-Weight on EOG Resources and lowered its price target to $147.
ticker_notes.NEM: Gold miners are eyeing their best month since April 2020, with several names already up 30% in August.
ticker_notes.ACN: Accenture was downgraded on the view that its headcount math shows the AI-decoupling story isn't yet proven.
ticker_notes.NOW: An expert cautioned that Salesforce's and ServiceNow's business models are in danger from AI disruption.
ticker_notes.NKE: Nike stock, down nearly 80% from its 2021 peak, drew Wall Street warnings of a 'Stage 4' technical breakdown.
ticker_notes.ADBE: Adobe fell as chip stocks cratered and bond yields bit, amid commentary that the market may take years to reward its AI efforts.
ticker_notes.AEP: Carl Icahn trimmed his AEP stake and Truist lowered its price target to $139 while maintaining Buy.
ticker_notes.ABBV: Wells Fargo maintained Overweight on AbbVie and raised its price target to $300.
ticker_notes.AIG: Cantor Fitzgerald maintained Overweight on AIG while lowering its price target to $90.
